purpose: Predicted batch-1 (b1) events that fall outside every video sidecar's wallclock window. Reproduction: take the b2 phase sequence from datasets/2026-02-04 11-08-51.json, scale each event's gap to b2-e10 by 0.9021 (= 70/77.6 SCADA-trace point-count ratio, operator-measured), and offset backwards from observed b1-e00 @ 2026-02-04T11:46:10.

anchor.source: Observed in datasets/2026-02-04 11-08-51.json (the long batch-2 recording, first event annotated).

secondary_anchor.note: Observed empty event in b2 sidecar. Cross-check: observed discharge -> empty gap 20s, predicted 20 * 0.9021 = 18s, Δ = -2s.

caveats: Linear inter-event scaling is a first-order approximation but holds remarkably well on the only directly-comparable phase: observed b1 discharge -> empty gap is 20s vs b2's 20s (ratio 1.0000); the global 0.902 scale predicts 18s, off by only 2s. This validates using the 0.9021 factor uniformly across phases as a first cut, but a per-phase scale calibration will be needed before any quantitative claim depends on the exact predicted wallclock of a non-observed event.

Clip filenames (e.g. '2026-02-05 10-18-50.mp4') and the DVR-burnt date overlay are both unreliable — the camera/DVR clock had a wrong DATE field. HH:MM:SS ran true relative to the SCADA wallclock. Per operator, the clips' actual recording date is 2026-02-04 (the same day as the long batch-2 recording), and every wallclock here is rendered on that date.
All clips fall entirely inside b1's 'boiling' phase; zero predicted transitions fall inside any clip.
